title: Support macro/snippet template standardization (required fields + KB linking)
creator: Dev Patel
project: CS & Support Escalation Playbook Refresh + Known-Issues Sprint (Q1 2026)
content:
## Context
Support escalations over the last quarter show repeated back-and-forth for the same few issues (streaming disconnects/timeouts, 429/quota confusion, Dedicated autoscaling oscillation, Private upgrade stuck migrations, audit log lag). We are publishing validated workarounds into the KB, but we still lose time because:
- macros/snippets are inconsistent in structure and tone (some read like internal notes; others are missing next steps)
- macros don’t consistently ask for the minimum diagnostics (region/model/request IDs/SDK version)
- macros don’t link to the canonical KB article or severity/escalation guidance

This ticket standardizes the **Support macro/snippet format** used in Jira SUP tickets (and any outbound customer comms copied from them), and defines a lightweight adoption checklist.

## Goals
- Make macros copy/paste-ready, customer-safe, and consistently structured.
- Ensure every macro includes the same required diagnostic asks and clear next steps.
- Drive KB discovery/deflection by linking to the Known Issues Index + specific workaround article.
- Reduce time-to-triage and time-to-mitigation for repeat issues; reduce “what do you need from us?” loops.

Non-goals
- Replace tiered SLA policy language (owned in PM-912).
- Rewrite the full escalation playbook (already in Confluence).
- Long-form training program; we’ll use quick-reference + reviews.

## Proposed Standard Macro Template (v1)
Each macro is a short, structured message that is safe to send to a customer. Internal-only details (dashboard links, suspected RCA, vendor references) must be separated.

### 1) Macro header (single line)
**Title:** <Symptom> — <Likely cause category> — <Primary next action>
Example: “Streaming resets mid-generation — client/network timeout — enable retry + adjust keepalive”

### 2) Acknowledge + restate (2–3 sentences)
- Confirm what we understand
- Confirm immediate intent (stabilize, mitigate, gather data)

### 3) Quick checks (customer action) — bullets
- 3–6 bullets maximum
- Use imperative verbs; include safe defaults
- If customer action is optional, label it clearly

### 4) Required diagnostics (copy/paste block)
Always include the following prompts (unless explicitly not applicable):
- **Region:** (e.g., us-east, eu-west)
- **Model + version:** (e.g., redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2026-01-28)
- **Endpoint:** (chat/completions, embeddings, rerank)
- **SDK + version:** (Python/TS/Go + exact version)
- **Request IDs + UTC timestamps:** (3–5 examples is ideal)
- **Sample error text / HTTP status:** (verbatim)
- **Client environment:** (language/runtime, proxy/load balancer, HTTP/2 on/off)

### 5) “If this is urgent” escalation guidance
Add a short, consistent line that references the rubric without re-litigating priority:
- “If this is blocking production or causing widespread errors, tell us and we’ll treat it as a P0/P1 and start an escalation bridge.”

### 6) Canonical KB links
- Always include:
  - Known Issues Index landing page
  - The specific workaround article (if one exists)
- If no KB article exists yet, include a placeholder line: “We’re drafting a Known Issue entry; in the meantime, steps above are the recommended mitigation.”

### 7) Internal-only section (clearly marked)
This is **not customer-facing** and stays in Jira internal comments:
- dashboard links
- current hypothesis / related incidents
- ownership + whether SRE is paged
- mapping to ENG/PM issues

## Required fields for macros
To prevent “macro drift”, every macro must include:
- Acknowledge + restate
- Quick checks
- Required diagnostics block
- Escalation guidance line
- KB links (index + specific article when available)

## Standard tone rules
- Avoid promising ETAs unless confirmed by SRE/Eng.
- Avoid blaming customer environment; frame as “to narrow down”.
- Prefer “recommended next step” over “you must”.
- Keep it readable (no more than ~200–250 words before diagnostics block).

## Rollout / Adoption checklist (Support)
Owner: Dev Patel (Support Ops) + Priya Shah (workflow + KB)

1) Inventory + pruning
- Confirm canonical macro list and delete/merge duplicates.
- Tag each macro to a primary issue category (Streaming, Rate limits/quota, Dedicated autoscaling, Private upgrades, Audit logs, Auth/SSO, Billing/usage).

2) Update top 10 macros first
- Use ticket volume list from “Top Support Issues Q1 2026”.
- Ensure each macro has correct KB link and “when to escalate” line.

3) Reviewer sign-off
- Docs/DevEx: Elliot Price + (Wei Chen for Hosted; Kira Thompson for Dedicated/Private)
- SRE spot-check of escalation line alignment: Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes

4) Where macros live
- Source of truth: Google Drive “support-macros-and-snippets-refresh”
- Published internal reference: Confluence Support Process page

5) Add links in workflows
- Jira triage checklist should prompt linking a macro + KB article when issue matches known issue.
- For new issues, macro must include diagnostics block and a “we’ll follow up with a KB entry if this becomes a known issue.”

6) Team enablement (30 minutes)
- Short walkthrough in #support: what changed, how to pick the right macro, what’s required.
- Pin the template and examples.

7) Measurement (post-sprint)
- % of SUP tickets with request IDs + region captured in first response
- repeat ticket rate for top 5 issues
- time-to-triage for P0/P1 tickets

## References / Cross-links
- Confluence: Support triage intake checklist (required fields)
- Confluence: Severity matrix + escalation triggers
- Confluence: Known issues index
- Drive: support-macros-and-snippets-refresh (source doc)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Template v1 approved by Support Ops + Docs
- [ ] Top 10 macros migrated to v1 format and reviewed
- [ ] Each migrated macro includes Known Issues Index link + specific article where applicable
- [ ] Diagnostics block standardized (fields listed above)
- [ ] Internal-only section guidance added (what not to email)
- [ ] Adoption checklist posted and pinned for Support
comments: 2026-02-06 (Dev Patel): Drafted template v1. Biggest gap today is missing request IDs + timestamps; causes delays when SRE asks for correlation. Priya Shah to integrate the diagnostics block into macros by default.

2026-02-08 (Elliot Price): +1 on separating customer-safe vs internal-only. Please avoid including dashboard links in the customer macro text; keep those as Jira internal notes only. Suggest adding a one-line ‘when to escalate’ section rather than describing P0/P1 in detail.

2026-02-10 (Sean Gallagher): Escalation line should not imply paging SRE automatically. Wording suggestion: ‘If production is blocked or error rate is widespread, confirm severity and we’ll initiate an escalation bridge per our incident process.’

2026-02-12 (Priya Shah): Updated 6 macros (Streaming timeouts, Streaming resets, 429 quota mismatch, Dedicated autoscaling oscillation, Private installer stuck migrations, Audit log delivery latency). Pending: ensure each one links to the final KB URL after publish.

2026-02-14 (Kira Thompson): Dedicated/Private macros need a reminder about redacting logs before sharing. Can we add a single line in the diagnostics block: ‘Please redact secrets (API keys, tokens) before sending logs.’

2026-02-15 (Dev Patel): Action: post template + examples to #support and pin. Next: coordinate with Dylan Brooks on Jira automation prompting the diagnostics block when creating SUP tickets (tracked separately).
